description:
Issue summary:
A recent canary rollout of rw-v2-large:2026-03-01-variantB caused automated quality-based fallback for several pinned routes. Investigation shows the canary introduces a tokenization delta (subtle BPE merge differences) that changes token boundaries for control/prompt tokens used by the customer's templates. The quality detector flagged regenerated output mismatches and triggered fallback; during the fallback process some pinned sessions were migrated off the pinned variant (pin migration) resulting in mixed-model responses for pinned customers.

Impact:
- Customer BrightWrite Analytics (enterprise) reported inconsistent outputs for pinned routes; timestamps show model switching mid-session for some long-lived sessions.
- User-facing generation differences led to downstream processing errors for their post-processing pipelines (JSON parse failures).
- Approx 1200 requests across two routes experienced mid-response variant switch over a 45-minute window.

Environment:
- Production, us-east region.
- Affected route names: /v1/chat/batch/brightwrite-report, /v1/generate/brightwrite-extract
- Canary: rw-v2-large:2026-03-01-variantB (canary weight 12% at time of incident)
- Stable pinned variant: rw-v2-large:2026-02-15-stable

Steps to reproduce:
1) Use customer prompt template including multi-line system instructions and control tokens (e.g., "<|prompt_section|>").
2) Send long-context sessions (>1024 tokens) pinned to rw-v2-large:2026-02-15-stable.
3) Trigger canary traffic split (weighted rollout including customers).
4) Observe output tokens where control tokens are tokenized differently by variantB and then fallback is applied by quality detector.

Observed behavior:
- Quality monitor detects BLEU/EM/JSON-parse regressions and triggers automated fallback to stable.
- Routing logs show the fallback decision was executed but pin migration process did not respect session affinity for a subset of session tokens, causing in-flight sessions to be redirected mid-response.
- Customers observed mixtures of new-variant and stable-variant outputs in the same session.

Expected behavior:
- Quality fallback should respect explicit model pins: pinned sessions must remain routed to the pinned model unless a manual override is requested.
- Automated quality checks should ignore purely tokenization-level deltas that do not change semantic output unless they break contract (e.g., structured-output parsing).

Logs / trace ids:
- routing::request_id=ff7a1d2b-3c44-4f1e-b6a8-9d1f9b3e72aa
- quality-monitor::event=qm-20260310-0201
- serving-runtime::worker=grind-rt-11 logs attached in GH PR 1882

Initial investigation summary:
- Reproduced tokenization difference locally using the two variants. VariantB splits the control token sequence "<|prompt_section|>" into ["<|prompt", "_section|>"] while stable keeps it as a single token. This shifts subsequent token indices and changes the exact byte-level output that the quality detector compares.
- The quality detector uses a lightweight string-compare heuristic on canonicalized outputs; the token boundary change triggers the heuristic even though human-readability and semantic content are preserved in most cases.
- Fallback action performs a routing table update that includes a pin-migration step. Pin migration logic relied on session-key hashing plus last-seen-edge metadata; under high concurrency there was a race that allowed in-flight requests to slip past affinity checks.

Workaround provided to customer:
- We temporarily disabled auto-fallback for the two affected routes for BrightWrite while we perform targeted fixes.
- Customer was offered a configuration to pin to exact variant full identifier (variant digest) rather than logical model tag; they accepted the temporary pin to rw-v2-large:2026-02-15-stable-digest:sha256:abcd1234 which prevented further mid-session migration.

Next steps / proposed remediation:
1) Hotfix serving-runtime to make fallback respect explicit pins and freeze session affinity for the lifetime of in-flight requests (patch queued: PR 1882).
2) Update quality-monitor heuristics to add a "tokenization-delta" pre-check that suppresses fallback for pure token boundary changes unless downstream contract parsing fails (conservative mode).
3) Add model-onboarding compatibility checks to detect tokenization differences between variants and flag them during the rollout approval step.
4) Add a regression test that simulates control-token boundary shifts and validates fallback suppression when semantic equivalence is preserved.

Customer communication:
- BrightWrite CS was notified at 2026-03-10 15:42 UTC; interim email sent with workaround and escalation path.

Resolution notes (in progress):
- Patch created and under code review for routing affinity fix.
- Quality-monitor change scoped and a/B test planned on staging.
comments: 2026-03-10 16:05 - Maya Chen (Support): Logged after BrightWrite engineering submitted examples where their JSON extractor failed mid-stream. Attached sample prompts + response diffs.
2026-03-10 17:22 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Confirmed tokenization delta locally. Adding serving-runtime and routing on-call. Filed PR 1882 to enforce pin affinity during fallback.

2026-03-11 09:14 - Priya Nair (Applied ML): Ran tokenizer diffs across RW-V2 variants; flagged variants created by retrain pipeline that changed BPE merges. Propose onboarding check to compare tokenization hashes.
2026-03-11 12:40 - Customer (BrightWrite - Alex Ramos): Confirmed enabling exact-variant pin prevents further mixed outputs. Awaiting permanent fix. Appreciative of quick workaround.
2026-03-12 10:05 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Deployed a canary patch to preserve session-affinity on fallback in staging; no regressions observed. Scheduling prod rollout after QA window.

2026-03-13 15:50 - Maya Chen (Support): Updated customer with timeline: hotfix targeted for 2026-03-14 morning US-east maintenance window. Advised that quality-monitor tokenization suppression will be a slower roll (design doc pending).
workaround: Disabled auto-fallback for affected routes for the customer and pinned to exact variant digest. Advised customer to avoid exposing new variant to their pinned routes until fix is deployed.
root_cause: Tokenization/BPE merge differences between the canary variant and the pinned stable variant caused string-level heuristics in the quality detector to fire. During the fallback routine, pin-migration code had a race that allowed in-flight sessions to be redirected, violating session affinity.
resolution: Hotfix PR 1882 enforces frozen session-affinity for in-flight requests during fallback. Quality-monitor will be updated to add tokenization-delta suppression before triggering fallback; onboarding checks for tokenization compatibility will be added. Work is in progress and scheduled for production deployment 2026-03-14 after QA.
